note: Character register modes (Alexander, 2026-08-31): what the character IS in the frame. Subsumes the retired authenticity dial (documentary->authentic, stylized->costume, cinematic->none). Per mode: sentence_pool = direct identification sentences (Alexander's design), wear = multipliers on the wear-state leans, marks = scar/marks probability multiplier, uniform_p + uniform_label = the role full-rig coin, family_wear = per-wardrobe-family wear overrides keyed to character_wardrobe.json families (the prestige fix: fine families keep their clothes even at authentic), exaggeration_pool = cartoon-only second sentence. Sentences draw LAST: register=none consumes no draws and reproduces the plain sheet byte-for-byte. Sentence language principle (Alexander, 2026-08-31, final): authentic is the generator's default assumption for a realistic outfit, so its sentence is a minimal marker only - which also anchors the character against style bleed in illustrated scenes. Explicit clarification belongs to the non-default registers (costume: 'their apparel is a costume version of ...'). Physical manifestation lives in the wear tilts, which adapt per wardrobe family via family_wear. Non-default marking is generalized - the sentence states what the register means for any outfit: costume recasts it as a replica, pulp as hero drama. No class presumptions (pirate, businessman, scientist alike).
